content.text:
The live evidence is consistent enough to separate “observed behavior” from “supported contract”:

- PRs #214, #216, and #220 were automatically re-reviewed across multiple pushed SHAs.
- Clean PRs #217, #219, and #221 ended with a new `+1` reaction and no Codex review object.
- PR #216 itself disproved guaranteed auto-start: its first review did not begin until an `@codex review` request.
- Codex review submissions are `COMMENTED`, not GitHub `APPROVED`; the thumbs-up is a PR reaction. So this is a repository-policy gate, not a native branch-protection approval.

I’ve also found one coverage gap: checking only `reviewThreads` can miss Codex feedback in the PR conversation or review body.

## Verdict

The workflow is thoughtful, but [AGENTS.md step 11](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/AGENTS.md:187) is not fully correct as written.

The important corrections are:

- “It reviews every push” is too absolute. Recent PRs show that Codex usually re-reviews pushed revisions, but [PR #216](https://github.com/scottdensmore/travel-app/pull/216) needed an explicit `@codex review` before its first review began. Official documentation guarantees the manual trigger and configurable automatic reviews, not re-reviewing every push. Add a timeout and manual-trigger fallback. [Official Codex GitHub documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/integrations/github/)

- “A 👍 you watched arrive” is good protection against stale reactions, but the gate should also record the expected head SHA and a UTC cutoff. Immediately before merging, re-fetch the PR and require:
  - unchanged head SHA;
  - a new Codex `+1` reaction after the cutoff/current review run;
  - no unresolved Codex threads;
  - no unaddressed Codex conversation comments or review-body findings.

- `reviewThreads` is necessary but not sufficient. It covers inline threads and their resolution state, but Codex can also post PR conversation comments and review-body feedback. Inspect all three surfaces: conversation comments, review submissions, and paginated `reviewThreads`.

- The thumbs-up is a PR reaction, not a GitHub approval review. Live Codex reviews here have state `COMMENTED`, not `APPROVED`. Therefore “gates the merge” is an AGENTS.md policy gate, not a GitHub-enforced branch-protection gate. The official documentation also says Codex guidance does not replace branch protections or required approvals.

- Change “Treat P1 as blocking” to “Treat P0 and P1 as blocking; answer every actionable lower-priority finding.” Recent PRs #214, #216, and #220 received P2 findings despite current documentation saying GitHub review focuses on P0/P1.

I recommend replacing the opening sentence with:

> Automatic Codex review is enabled for this repository and has been observed to rerun after pushes, but never treat silence as approval. After each push, record the expected PR head SHA and wait for a new review run. If Codex does not start promptly, comment `@codex review`.

Then make the final gate explicitly require an unchanged recorded SHA, fresh post-cutoff `+1`, and complete inspection of all feedback surfaces.

No files were changed. Local `main` remains clean and synchronized with `origin/main`.

I am not sure what the +1 is about

`+1` is GitHub’s API name for the 👍 reaction.

So:

- GitHub UI displays: 👍
- `gh api .../reactions` returns: `"content": "+1"`

For the Codex bot, that reaction means it completed the review without suggestions. It is not a numeric score or a formal GitHub `APPROVED` review—just the bot’s clean-review signal.
I also don't think we should do the @codex review because then we could double up

Agreed. An automatic review may already be queued even before 👀 appears, so posting `@codex review` could produce duplicate runs and duplicate findings.

The safer workflow is:

> Automatic Codex review is expected after each push. Wait for a new 👀 followed by 👍 or review findings. Silence is pending, never approval. If no review arrives, stop and report the merge as blocked; do not post `@codex review` unless the user explicitly requests it.

That removes the unsupported “reviews every push” guarantee without risking duplicate reviews.

I’ll make the narrow documentation change we agreed on: automatic review remains the expected path, silence remains pending, and agents must not post `@codex review` unless you explicitly request it. I’m rechecking the current official Codex wording first, then I’ll create a documentation branch and edit only that workflow section.

Official OpenAI documentation distinguishes configurable automatic reviews from the separate manual `@codex review` trigger, so the repository can safely prohibit agents from invoking the manual path. `main` is current, clean, and there are no open PRs; I’m creating the documentation branch now.
